bibl.title: God's Library. The Archaeology of the Earliest Christian Manuscripts.
bibl.seg: Brent Nongbri, God's Library. The Archaeology of the Earliest Christian Manuscripts.
New Haven, Yale University Press, 2018, xii-403 pp., figg. ISBN 978-0-300-21541-0. $35.

C.R. par Mark Letteney, Journal of Late Antiquity 12 (2019) pp. 550-552. - Anne Boud'hors, ChrEg 95 (2020) No. 189, pp. 174-177. - Steven M. Stannish, AJA 124 (2020) Online Book Reviews < https://www.ajaonline.org/book-review/4039 >. - Donatella Tronca, BMCRev < https://bmcr.brynmawr.edu/2020/2020.05.02 >.
bibl.note: Prologue: Reintroducing the earliest Christian manuscripts. - 1. The early Christian book. - 2. The dating game. - 3. Finding early Christian books. - 4. A discovery "which threw all others in the shade": the Beatty Biblical papyri. - 5. An elusive collection: the Bodmer papyri. - 6. Excavating Christian litter and literature at Oxyrhynchus. - 7. Fabricating a second-century codex of the four Gospels. - Epilogue: The future of ancient Christian books. - Appendix: Christian books from Oxyrhynchus. - Notes. Bibliography. Indexes.
